exposure: CONUT score calculation according to two different cut-off values
cohort: 141 pregnant women in the 32nd-37th gestational weeks, 62 with late-onset FGR and 79 controls with pre-pregnancy BMI <25 kg/m2, without systemic/metabolic disease, substance use, or medication use
finding: OPNI and CONUT scores, used to predict nutritional status and prognosis in cancer and chronic diseases, were not useful in predicting late-onset FGR.
mod_finding: The vaginal birth rate was higher in the control group (67.1% vs. 32.9%), and the cesarean section rate was higher in patients with late-onset FGR (58.1% vs. 41.9%).
